10:2: And so that you may relate before your son and grandson the miracles that I performed in Egypt,
and the miraculous signs I performed among them.
You will then know that I am Adonoy.”
10:3: Moshe and Aharon went in to Pharaoh
and they said to him, “This is what Adonoy, God of the Hebrews, has said,
Send My people out that they may worship before Me.
10:5: They will cover the eye of the sun of the land
so that one will be unable to see the land.
They will eat all that was spared, that remained for you from the hail,
and they will eat every tree
that grows for you in the field.
10:8: Moshe and Aharon were brought back to Pharaoh,
10:9: “With our young and with our old we will go.
With our sons, with our daughters, with our sheep and with our cattle we will go,
for it is a festival before Adonoy for all of us.”
10:10: He [Pharaoh] said to them, “So be it. May the Word of Adonoy be your support
just as I will send you and your little ones.
Beware the evil which you intend to commit will be turned against your faces.
10:11: This is not right. [Only] the [adult] men should go and worship before Adonoy
for this is what you desire.”
10:15: They covered the eye of the sun of the entire land so that the land was darkened.
They ate all the vegetation of the land, and all the fruit of the trees
that was left [spared] by the hail.
No greenery remained on the trees or on the vegetation of the field in the entire land of Egypt.
10:16: and he said, “I have sinned before Adonoy, your God, and to you.
10:17: Now forgive my sin just this one time
10:21: Adonoy said to Moshe, “Stretch out your hand toward the sky,
and there will be darkness over the land of Egypt
after the darkness of the night will be removed.
10:24: Pharaoh called to Moshe, and he said, “Go! Worship before Adonoy.
Just let your sheep and cattle stay behind.
Even your little ones can go with you.”
10:25: “You too will give us sacrifices and burnt-offerings
that we will make [offer] before Adonoy our God.
10:26: Our own flocks will also go with us. Not a single thing will remain.
since we do not know with what [animals] we will worship before Adonoy
10:29: I will not see your face again.”
11:2: and let each man request [borrow] from his friend, and each woman from her friend,
articles of silver and articles of gold.”
11:4: I will become revealed in the midst of Egypt.
11:5: Every first-born in the land of Egypt will die,
from the first-born of Pharaoh who is destined to sit upon the throne of his kingdom,
to the first-born of the [Egyptian] slave girl,
11:7: But among all the B’nei Yisrael, a dog will not cause damage with its tongue [growl]
11:8: Then all these, your servants, will come down to me, and beseech me saying, ‘Go! You and all the people that are with you.
He [Moshe] then left Pharaoh in great anger.
11:9: Thus I will multiply My wonders in the land of Egypt.”
12:4: If the [members of the] household are too few for the numbering of the lamb
then he shall take [a lamb] [together] with his neighbor, close by his house, according to the number of individuals.
According to what the person eats
shall you make your count regarding the lamb.
12:8: They shall eat the meat during this night.
It shall be roasted over fire. They shall eat it with matzoh
12:9: You must not eat it half-cooked
its head with its knees and its inner organs.
12:11: This is how you must eat it:
and your staff in your hand.
You must eat it in haste,
12:12: I will become revealed in the land of Egypt on that night,
and I will strike [kill] every first-born in the land of Egypt,
and against all the gods of Egypt, I will execute judgments, I am Adonoy.
12:13: The blood will be for you as a sign on the houses where you are [staying].
and I will have mercy upon you.
There will be no plague against you
when I strike the land of Egypt.
12:14: This day shall be for you a [day of] remembrance.
You shall celebrate it as a festival before Adonoy,
throughout your generations. It is an eternal statute that you must celebrate it.
12:15: You must eat matzoh for seven days,
you must nullify [all] leaven from your homes;
for anyone who eats chametz, that soul will be cut off from Yisrael.
[Chametz is forbidden] from the first day [of Pesach] until [after] the seventh day.
12:17: You must be vigilant regarding the matzoh,
I brought out your hosts from the land of Egypt.
You must preserve this day for your generations, it is an eternal statute.
12:18: In Nisan on the fourteenth day of the month, in the evening
until the twenty-first day of the month in the evening.
12:20: You must not eat anything that is chametz.
12:22: Take a bunch of hyssop, and dip it in the blood that is in the basin.
Sprinkle the lintel and the two side [door] posts
with some of the blood in the basin.
And all of you, let no man go out the door of his house until morning.
12:23: Adonoy will become revealed to plague the Egyptians
and He will see the blood on the lintel
and on the two side [door] posts.
Adonoy will then have mercy upon that door
and will not allow the destroyer
to enter your houses to plague you.
12:27: You shall say, “It is the Pesach-offering of compassion before Adonoy Who had mercy upon the houses of the B’nei Yisrael in Egypt
when He struck the Egyptians and saved our homes.
The people then bowed and prostrated themselves.
12:29: It was [exactly] midnight and Adonoy struck down [killed] every first-born son in the land of Egypt,
from the first-born son of Pharaoh who is destined to sit upon the throne of his kingdom,
to the first-born son of the captive [prisoner]
as well as every first-born animal.
12:31: [Pharaoh] called for Moshe and Aharon that night and said, “Set out! Get out from among my people,
both you and the B’nei Yisrael.
Go worship before Adonoy as you have said [requested].
12:32: Take your sheep and cattle too, as you have said and go;
12:34: The people took their dough before it was leavened.
The leftovers of their dough were wrapped in their clothing, [and carried] on their shoulders.
12:38: A great multitude of strangers also went up with them.
12:42: This was a night of vigil before Adonoy,
to bring them out of the land of Egypt.
This night remains a night of vigil before Adonoy
for all the B’nei Yisrael for [all] their generations.
12:43: Adonoy said to Moshe and Aharon,
“This is the statute of the Pesach offering:
No Jew who renounces his religion may eat it.
12:46: It must be eaten in one group.
You must not remove from the house any of its flesh, to the outdoors,
and you must not break any of its bones.
12:48: When a proselyte dwells with you and wants to make the Pesach-offering before Adonoy,
every male must be circumcised. He may then come near [join] to make it,
and be like the native born.
But no uncircumcised male may eat of it.
13:2: “Sanctify before Me all the first-born, that [is the first to] open the womb among the B’nei Yisrael,
13:5: When Adonoy brings you to the land of the Canaanite, the Chittites, the Emorites, the Chivites and the Yevusites, which He swore to your fathers [that He would] give to you —
you must conduct this service in this month.
13:6: For seven days you must eat the matzoh,
13:7: No chametz may be seen in your possession, and no leaven may be seen in all your boundaries.
13:12: [At that time] you must pass on, [set aside] every one that [is first to] open the womb, before Adonoy.
Every firstling that is dropped [born] by animals that belong to you, the males shall be consecrated before Adonoy.
13:15: When Pharaoh stubbornly refused to send us out,
Adonoy killed every first-born in the land of Egypt,
from the first-born of man to the first-born of beast.
I am therefore sacrificing before Adonoy all that [is first to] open the womb which are male,
and the first-born of my sons I redeem.’
13:16: [These words] shall be a sign on your hand
Adonoy brought us out of Egypt.”
